_note: Our own writing: the pirate career for AI-GM play. Canon-consistent: pirates and boarding (Core p.42, p.126, p.139), NHPs and cascade (p.107), cloning and flash cloning (p.83-84), Union DoJ/HR. Nothing from Massif's modules. All text here is easy to edit; the engine (CampaignScript) reads it. Branches: b1 the mutiny, b2 MERIDIAN, b3 the start, b4 the first raid, b5 Hask's cut, b6 the Gallowglass, b6r Vosk's fate, b7 the breach, b8 Ruslan Dey, b9 the amnesty, b10 Saltmarrow, b11 the crews, b12 MERIDIAN's fate, b13 the captaincy, b14 Hask's fate, b15 the big score, b16 betrayal, b17 the final site, b18 the ending. Splits (decisions): the mutiny and the captaincy. After the prologue the Cadence is home to a whole society (Hask's people from the Gannet, ship-borne like a colony ship, Core p.10, p.20): the squad's renown with them, Hask quietly cutting it down to keep the peace, and the unrest that causes drive the mutiny as much as hardship does (society, ShipLife).
name: Dead Reckoning
premise: You're the lance aboard the Saint Cadence, an IPS-N long-hauler stalled on a fringe run. Her NHP is failing, the company says wait four months, and the crew has stopped waiting. Soon the Cadence will be home to a whole people: Corvo Hask's ship-born families, their markets and feuds, and the captain who keeps the peace among them. Hask values his lancers. He just can't afford for them to be loved more than he is.

kell.name: Captain Idris Kell
kell.title: IPS-N master of the Saint Cadence

siddiqui.name: Mother Amara Siddiqui
siddiqui.title: Speaker for the families of the holds

p1_cascade.title: Cascade
intro: Day forty-one, adrift. The Saint Cadence is an IPS-N long-hauler on a fringe run, and her NHP, MERIDIAN, has started repeating itself: the same sentence, again and again, a little different each time.
IPS-N's orders: hold position and wait four months for a recovery tug. The crew has stopped waiting. You're the lance they hired to keep the cargo safe.
briefing: Lancers. MERIDIAN has lost the maintenance frames in the cargo spine. They're cutting through bulkheads, and they're heading for the reactor.
Stop them. Then come to the bridge. We have another problem.

hook.title: Cascade
hook.objective: Stop MERIDIAN's runaway maintenance frames in the cargo spine before they reach the reactor.
hook.stakes: If they reach the reactor, nobody goes home.
hook.question: Is it the NHP, or someone using it?

p2_meridian.title: MERIDIAN
intro: {p2_line}
Down in engineering, MERIDIAN's core room has sealed itself. The lights spell out the same word, over and over: STAY.

p2_line.text: The bridge belongs to Tamsin Reyes now. Captain Kell and his officers hold engineering, and they won't come out.
The mutiny broke on the bridge, but Tamsin Reyes and her people got away down the spine. They're holding engineering, and the core.

briefing: Whoever holds MERIDIAN's core holds the ship. Get in there.
And when you're in front of it, you'll have to decide what to do with it.

hook.title: The Core Room
hook.objective: Fight through engineering to MERIDIAN's core room.
hook.stakes: The NHP is failing, and whoever reaches it decides what happens to it.
hook.question: Stabilise it, cut it loose, or carry it out?

p3_answer.title: Someone Answers
intro: Somebody heard the Cadence's distress call. Not IPS-N: the Gannet, a patched-up raider hauler that has been home to three thousand people for two generations, with markets in her holds and children who've never seen a sky.
Her captain, Corvo Hask, has a voice on the comms like warm honey: "Saint Cadence, my ship is dying and yours has room. Let's talk."
briefing: Hask's boarding party is coming through the docking ring to make sure the talk goes his way. Whatever we decide about him, we decide it standing up.
Hold the ring.

hook.title: Someone Answers
hook.objective: Hold the docking ring against Hask's boarding party.
hook.stakes: If they take the ring, they take the ship.
hook.question: Do you fight Hask, or deal with him?

c4_raid.title: First Blood
intro: {start_line}

The Cadence is a town now: three thousand of Hask's people in her holds, market stalls in her cargo bays, laundry strung across the crew deck. Everyone works. The trade that feeds them all is raiding. "We take what the Union doesn't miss," Hask says. "And you, my lancers, are how we take it."

start_line.text: Nine days in a lifeboat with Captain Kell's officers, and then a broken-nosed hull blotting out the stars: Hask came back for you. "Pilots are pilots," he said. "I can always use more."
You reached Gallows Reach in a lifeboat that smelled of fear and coolant. The Cadence was docked there a week later, under Hask's colours. He was hiring.
Hask and Tamsin shook on it over Captain Kell's empty chair: the Gannet's people, the Cadence's hull, one crew.

briefing: A Harrison Armory supply freighter, the Brightwater, running light on escorts. Board her, take the hold.
And before you go: there's a vat in the medical bay. Everyone who works aboard gets a template in it. We've buried too many good people out here. This ship doesn't do that any more.

hook.title: First Blood
hook.objective: Board the freighter Brightwater and take her hold.
hook.stakes: Her crew are armed and frightened. How this goes is up to you.
hook.question: What happens to the freighter's crew?

loot.name: the Brightwater's cargo of reactor parts

lines.text: The Brightwater's crew are on their knees in her cargo bay, twenty of them. Somebody's crying.
Your prize, your call. Though I'll say: a crew that talks is a crew that tells the Union where three thousand of my people are sleeping.

choices.text: Put them in their lifeboats. They're no threat to anyone now.

effects.why: they let the Brightwater's crew go

choices.text: Hold them for ransom. Harrison Armory pays for its people.
Space them. No witnesses.

effects.why: the Brightwater's crew went out the airlock

c5_cut.title: Hask's Cut
intro: {raid_line}
Hask divides the take in the mess, in front of everyone. Half goes to the ship: food, air, the repair crews, the families in the holds. A fifth to the captain. A tenth to the lance.

raid_line.text: Nobody in the mess talks about the Brightwater's crew. Nobody looks at you, either.
Word gets around: the Cadence's lancers let a freighter crew go. Some of Hask's people think you've gone soft. Tamsin buys you a drink.
Harrison Armory paid the ransom inside a week. Hask is in a very good mood.

briefing: Next job: an ore barge with a manna safe aboard. In and out.
And then we'll talk about shares, if you're unhappy with yours. I hear some of you are.

hook.title: The Ore Barge
hook.objective: Hit the ore barge Kettle Creek and crack its manna safe.
hook.stakes: Half the crew is counting on this score.
hook.question: Who gets what from the take?

lines.text: Half for the ship, a fifth for the captain, a tenth for the lance. That keeps three thousand people fed and nobody fighting over the scraps.
If the lance wants more, it can tell the holds whose bread it's coming out of.

choices.text: Fine. Your ship, your cut.

agenda.why: a tenth for the lance while the lance does the bleeding

choices.text: The lance takes the hits. Every pilot gets a full crew share, or we stop flying.

effects.why: the lance stood up to the captain in the mess

choices.text: Whatever you say, captain.

c6_gallowglass.title: The Gallowglass
intro: Gallows Reach is a station built out of a dead mining hub, where nobody asks where a ship's been. It's also the Gallowglass's port: twelve raider ships under Commodore Vosk, and Vosk doesn't like newcomers.
Vosk wants a word with the Cadence. The word, it turns out, is a fleet.
briefing: Vosk's ships have the Cadence pinned at the station's outer moorings. They want a tithe, or a fight.
Break their hold on the moorings, or make them a better offer.

hook.title: The Gallowglass
hook.objective: Break the Gallowglass's hold on the outer moorings.
hook.stakes: If Vosk wins here, the Cadence pays him forever.
hook.question: Fight Vosk, deal with him, or sell Hask to him?

lines.text: Vosk's lieutenant finds you afterwards in a Gallows bar, alone. She slides a datachip across the table.
The Commodore has an offer. Join the Gallowglass, take a share of the Reach. Or tell us where Hask sleeps. Your choice.

choices.text: Tell Vosk the Cadence answers to nobody. We'll see him on the moorings again.

effects.why: the lance faced down Vosk's fleet

choices.text: We'll fly with the Gallowglass when it suits us. Draw up the terms.
Hask sleeps in the captain's quarters. Midnight, station time.

c7_breach.title: The Breach
intro: {sold_line}
Hask has a job that pays more than all the others put together: an IPS-N courier carrying the Cadence's own recovery orders, and every crew roster IPS-N has for her.

sold_line.text: Somebody came for Hask at midnight. He wasn't in his bunk. He's been smiling at you ever since.
The Gallowglass are watching the Cadence from every dock on the Reach.

briefing: We take the courier, we wipe her records, and nobody ever knows who we were.
If her escort comes back before we're done, someone holds the breach while the Cadence pulls away. That's what lancers are for.

hook.title: The Breach
hook.objective: Take the IPS-N courier, wipe her records, and get back aboard before her escort returns.
hook.stakes: Hask has already said who stays behind if it goes wrong.
hook.question: Who holds the breach?

lines.text: The escort came back early. Hask was already pulling the Cadence away from the courier, with the breach still open.
Lancer! Hold the breach two minutes. I'll bring her back for you, I swear it on my people.

choices.text: Go. I'll hold it.

agenda.why: Hask left them holding the breach

effects.why: a pilot held the breach for the ship

choices.text: Nobody stays behind. Bring the ship back, Hask, or I'll come and get it.
Tamsin, blow the courier's cargo hatch. We'll all come out that way.

c8_dey.title: The Hunter
intro: {rep_line}
A Union DoJ/HR bounty hunter has come to Gallows Reach asking about the Cadence. His name is Ruslan Dey, and he's never yet gone home without the people he came for.

rep_line.text: The Brightwater's lifeboats were found empty. Union news calls the Cadence's crew murderers, and it shows your mechs.
The Brightwater's crew told everyone the Cadence's lancers let them go. In the fringe bars, people drink to you.
The Cadence has a name now, on the Union's lists and in the fringe bars both.

briefing: Dey has hired local guns and he's waiting for us at the Reach's cargo locks.
Lure him in and take him, cut a deal, or run. Just don't let him take us.

hook.title: The Hunter
hook.objective: Face Ruslan Dey's hired guns at Gallows Reach's cargo locks.
hook.stakes: Dey has warrants for every one of you.
hook.question: Take him, deal with him, or run?

lines.text: You're better than your warrants say. So let's be honest with each other.
Help me take someone worse than you, and when it's over, you come in quietly. You'll get a fair trial. That's more than most people on my list get.

choices.text: Deal. When this is over, we come in.
Get off this station, Dey. Next time we won't let you walk.
Sure. Whatever you say.

c9_halloran.title: Amnesty
intro: IPS-N's recovery tug arrived at last, four months late and three systems behind you. Commander Ines Halloran followed the Cadence's trail to the Reach.
She doesn't want a fight. She wants her ship back, and the NHP that was in it.
briefing: Before we talk, prove you can still do honest work. Gallowglass raiders are stripping an IPS-N relay out past the Reach.
Clear them off, and I'll make you an offer.

hook.title: Amnesty
hook.objective: Clear the Gallowglass raiders off the IPS-N relay.
hook.stakes: Halloran is watching how you fight.
hook.question: Do you take IPS-N's offer?

lines.text: Bring me the Saint Cadence and MERIDIAN, and I'll sign a full amnesty for every pilot aboard. IPS-N will even keep you on.
Refuse, and the next ship you see from us will be a recovery squadron.

choices.text: We'll bring her home. Draw up the amnesty.
The Cadence isn't yours any more. Send your squadron.
Give me the papers. I'll need time to bring the crew round.

c10_colony.title: Saltmarrow
intro: Saltmarrow is a frozen colony at the edge of nowhere, a few thousand people and one water plant. The Cadence needs supplies. So does the Gallowglass, and they got here first.
Elder Yusra Pell meets you on the landing ice with her hands open.
briefing: The Gallowglass are taking our winter stores. If they take the water plant, we won't see spring.
Please. We can't pay you much.

hook.title: Saltmarrow
hook.objective: Drive the Gallowglass away from Saltmarrow's water plant.
hook.stakes: A few thousand people need that plant to see the spring.
hook.question: Do you protect Saltmarrow, or squeeze it yourself?

lines.text: You saved the plant. We'll give what we can spare.
What they can spare? Lancers, take the stores. All of them. We have a ship to feed.

choices.text: We take what they can spare, and we keep the Gallowglass off them.

effects.why: the lance stood up for Saltmarrow

choices.text: Take the stores. All of them.
Half. And Saltmarrow owes the Cadence a favour.

c11_factions.title: Two Crews
intro: The Cadence has two crews now: the old hands, who came aboard under IPS-N and follow Tamsin Reyes, and the Gannet's people, who follow Hask.
{people_line}
{grudge_line}

people_line.text: And down in the holds, people have started asking out loud why the captain keeps sending their protectors away.
The children in the holds play at being your lance. Hask has noticed.
Hask keeps the peace between them, mostly.

grudge_line.text: And everyone knows {aggrieved} has had enough. They've been saying it in the mess, loudly.
Fights in the mess have stopped being about cards.

briefing: A Gallowglass gunship is shadowing us. Hask wants it gone before it calls the rest of the fleet.
Take it down. And afterwards, Tamsin wants to talk to you. Privately.

hook.title: The Shadow
hook.objective: Destroy the Gallowglass gunship shadowing the Cadence.
hook.stakes: If it calls the fleet, the Cadence is surrounded.
hook.question: Which crew are you?

lines.text: Hask keeps the peace by keeping you small. Every time the holds cheer for the lance, he finds you a job on the far side of the ship and his own people take the credit.
People down there call you their protectors. He can't stand it. When it comes to it, and it will, whose side are you on?

choices.text: Yours. When you move, we move with you.
Hask keeps us paid and alive. I'm not starting a war in the mess.
I'm keeping my head down until I know who's going to win.
The holds don't want Hask's peace. They want us. Let's stop pretending otherwise.
I've eaten scraps and bled for a tenth while he takes half. I'm done waiting. I'll lead it.

c12_meridian.title: MERIDIAN Fails
intro: {m_line}

m_line.text: Hask salvaged MERIDIAN's core from where you cut it loose. It's been drifting in a cargo crate, talking to itself. It's getting worse.
MERIDIAN's core has been in a crate in your bunk since the Cadence. Lately it hums at night, and the lights flicker when it does.
MERIDIAN is getting worse. Doors open on their own. Twice, the Cadence's guns tracked Hask's own shuttle.

briefing: There's a parts broker on Gallows Reach with everything an NHP needs to hold together, and a fence called Marchetti with a blank casket in his locked hold.
Raid the broker's warehouse for parts. What you do with MERIDIAN after that is up to you.

hook.title: Parts
hook.objective: Raid the broker's warehouse on Gallows Reach for NHP parts.
hook.stakes: Without them, MERIDIAN won't last the month.
hook.question: Fix it, free it, replace it, or let it go?

loot.name: a crate of NHP casket parts

lines.text: I can feel myself coming apart. I remember the Cadence's first voyage and I can't remember your names.
What are you going to do with me?

choices.text: Hold still. We've got the parts. We're fixing you.
You've been in a box long enough. You're free: go where you like.
I'm sorry. We're letting you go.
We have a new casket. We're replacing you, MERIDIAN. I'm sorry.

c13_captaincy.title: The Captaincy
intro: {cap_line}

cap_line.text: You said it in front of the whole mess: you challenge Corvo Hask for the captain's chair. By the old law of the fringe ships, he has to answer it.
Hask's ledger is going round the crew deck: every pilot he's ever lost, and what he sold their templates for afterwards. The crew has gone very quiet.
{aggrieved} isn't waiting any longer. Tonight the old hands move on the bridge.
The holds have had enough of Hask's peace. Tonight Mother Siddiqui's families and the old hands move on the bridge together, and they've asked the lance to lead them.
Tonight the old hands move on the bridge. You're with them.

Tamsin Reyes has made her move without you. Her people have the hangar and they're coming for the bridge, and Hask is calling for his lancers: "Hold the bridge with me, and nobody aboard ever forgets it."

briefing: This is it. Whatever happens tonight, the Cadence has one captain by morning.

hook.title: Mutiny
hook.objective: Take the bridge from Hask's loyalists.
hook.stakes: Whoever holds the bridge by morning holds the Cadence.
hook.question: Who commands the Saint Cadence?

variants.title: The Challenge
variants.objective: Beat Corvo Hask in single combat, in front of the crew.
variants.stakes: Win, and the chair is yours by the old law. Lose, and it's his forever.

variants.title: Tamsin's Mutiny
variants.objective: Hold the bridge for Hask against Tamsin's mutineers.

c14_score.title: The Big Score
intro: {captain_line}
{score_line}

captain_line.text: Hask sits in the captain's chair as if he never left it. "No hard feelings," he says. He means it, which is worse.
The captain's chair is a pilot's now. The crew salutes it, mostly.
Captain Tamsin Reyes walks the Cadence's decks like she's been doing it for years.
Captain Bede Okonkwo runs the Cadence like a ledger: carefully, and in the black.

score_line.text: The score: a Union-impounded convoy of printers, parked at Gallows Reach's customs dock while DoJ/HR argues over the paperwork.
The score: the Gallowglass treasury, in Commodore Vosk's strongroom at the heart of Gallows Reach.

briefing: One last job, and everyone aboard can stop running.
Take it.

hook.title: The Big Score
hook.objective: Hit the Gallowglass treasury in Vosk's strongroom.
hook.stakes: This is the score that ends the running, one way or another.
hook.question: Does the Cadence get away with it?

variants.title: The Big Score
variants.objective: Steal the impounded printer convoy from Gallows Reach's customs dock.

lines.text: It's done. It's in the hold. I've counted it twice and I still don't believe it.

choices.text: Count it a third time. Then we'll see who comes for it.
Shares for everyone aboard. Full shares.

c15_final_hunt.title: Warrants
intro: Ruslan Dey has come back to Gallows Reach with Union marshals and a warrant with every one of your names on it. The station's docks are sealed.
There's no talking your way out of this one.
briefing: They've sealed the docks. Fight through to the Cadence or don't leave at all.

hook.title: Warrants
hook.objective: Fight through Dey's hunters and the Union marshals to the Cadence's berth.
hook.stakes: Everything you've done is on that warrant.
hook.question: Does anyone get off Gallows Reach?

c15_final_recovery.title: Recovery
intro: {rec_line}

rec_line.text: Commander Halloran has read the papers you never signed. Her recovery squadron is alongside, and her boarders are cutting through the hull.
Commander Halloran keeps her promises. An IPS-N recovery squadron has the Cadence surrounded, and her boarders are cutting through the hull.

briefing: They're aboard. This is our ship. Hold her.

hook.title: Recovery
hook.objective: Hold the Saint Cadence against IPS-N's recovery boarders.
hook.stakes: Lose, and the Cadence goes home without you.
hook.question: Who does the Saint Cadence belong to?

c15_final_gallow.title: The Gallowglass Fleet
intro: {gal_line}

gal_line.text: Commodore Vosk wants his treasury back, and he's brought all twelve ships to ask for it. His flagship has the Cadence grappled.
With the Cadence going straight, the Gallowglass mean to take her before IPS-N can. Vosk's flagship has her grappled.

briefing: We go across to Vosk's flagship and end this on his deck.

hook.title: The Gallowglass Fleet
hook.objective: Board Commodore Vosk's flagship and break the Gallowglass.
hook.stakes: If Vosk's flagship falls, the Gallowglass fall with it.
hook.question: Who rules the Reach?

endings.title: Lost with the Cadence
endings.text: The last fight went the wrong way. The Saint Cadence drifts dark at the edge of the Reach, and the fringe bars tell three different stories about how her lancers died. None of them are true. All of them are better than the truth.

endings.title: Hask's Expendables
endings.text: Corvo Hask keeps the ship, and the peace. The lance had become too loved for a captain to live with: at Gallows Reach he thanks you in front of the whole ship, gives you your mechs and a fair share, and sets you ashore. The holds never quite forgive him. The Cadence sails on without her protectors.

endings.title: Brought to Trial
endings.text: Ruslan Dey keeps his word, and so do you. The trial on a Union court world lasts a month. You testify against the Gallowglass, against Hask, against yourselves. The sentence is lighter than anyone expected. Dey is in the gallery every day.

endings.title: The Monster the Union Had to Stop
endings.text: They tell stories about the Cadence's lancers now: the crew of the Brightwater, the stores of Saltmarrow. Union DoJ/HR put your faces on every gate in the region. Whether the Union caught you or not, the story ends the same way: as a warning.

endings.title: Go Legit
endings.text: Commander Halloran signs the amnesty on the Cadence's bridge. IPS-N takes back its ship, and takes on its lancers. A year later, you're flying escort on a fringe run like the one where it all started. Sometimes you see the Reach on the scopes.

endings.title: MERIDIAN's Children
endings.text: MERIDIAN chose to stay. The Saint Cadence is a ship with a mind of her own now, and she picks her crew: the frightened, the hunted, the ones nobody else will take. Nobody owns her. She's the first free ship on the Reach, and not the last.

endings.title: Captains of a Free Fleet
endings.text: With the Gallowglass treasury and the Gallowglass broken, the Reach's ships needed someone to follow. They chose the Cadence. There's a free fleet on the fringe now, with a charter and a vote and no captain who's afraid of his own heroes.

endings.title: Legend of the Fringe
endings.text: Saltmarrow named its new water plant after the Cadence. The Brightwater's crew still drink to you. On the fringe, where the Union's law is thin, people say the Cadence's lancers will come if you call. Sometimes, you do.

endings.title: Retire Rich
endings.text: The score was enough. More than enough. The lance scatters across the fringe with new names and full accounts: a bar on a quiet moon, a ranch, a small ship of your own. Nobody ever finds out who you were. That was the point.

open.speaker: narrator
line: When you get back to the bridge, it's already happening. Tamsin Reyes and twenty of the crew have the hatch. Captain Kell has a sidearm and four officers.

tamsin.speaker: npc
line: Four months waiting on a tug, with an NHP that's losing its mind? I'm taking us to Gallows Reach. Lancers: you with us, or with him?

kell.speaker: Captain Kell
line: This is mutiny, Reyes. IPS-N hangs mutineers. Lancers, you're under contract to me. Do your job.

ask.speaker: npc
line: Well?

choices.text: Tamsin's right. Nobody's dying out here for a cargo manifest.

decision.prompt: Back Tamsin's mutiny against Captain Kell

choices.text: The captain gives the orders. Put it down, Reyes.

decision.prompt: Stand with Captain Kell against the mutiny

choices.text: We're not shooting anyone over this. Sort it out yourselves.

after_mutiny.speaker: narrator
line: The officers look at your mechs, and at each other. It's over before anyone fires.

after_loyal.speaker: narrator
line: Tamsin swears, and her people fall back down the spine. They'll be back.

after_aside.speaker: narrator
line: Without the lance, Kell's officers don't stand a chance. Tamsin takes the bridge. She doesn't thank you.

open.speaker: npc
line: Stay. Stay. I am sorry. I am trying to stop saying it. Stay.

ask.speaker: npc
line: Whatever you do, do it soon. I can feel the next loop coming.

choices.text: Talk to me, MERIDIAN. Keep talking while I lock your governors down.
I'm pulling your core. You'll be safe in the dark. So will we.
We're taking you with us. In a box, if we have to.

stable.speaker: npc
line: ...Thank you. It's quieter. It won't stay quiet.

cut.speaker: narrator
line: The core comes out with a sound like a held breath. The Cadence's lights go dim and stay dim.

box.speaker: narrator
line: MERIDIAN fits in a crate the size of a coffin. It hums all the way to your bunk.

open.speaker: npc
line: Good fight. Truly. You lot are wasted on a freight run.

offer.speaker: npc
line: Here's how it is. The Gannet won't last the year, and your Cadence has holds big enough for all my people. We're coming aboard, and there's a place for anyone who'll work: everyone works on my ship. The lifeboats are there for anyone who'd rather not.

choices.text: We stay with the Cadence. Wherever she goes.
We'll take our chances in the lifeboat.

stay.speaker: npc
line: Welcome aboard. We're a ship that looks after its own. You'll see.

boat.speaker: npc
line: Suit yourselves. The fringe is small. We'll meet again.

open.speaker: narrator
line: By morning the bridge is quiet. There's blood on the deck plates and the crew is waiting to hear who's in charge.

tamsin_won.speaker: npc
line: Hask's in the brig. The Cadence is mine. You fought for him, and you fought well. Fly for me now, or get off at the Reach.

loyal.speaker: Hask
line: You held. I won't forget it. And Tamsin... well. We'll see what she's good for in the brig.

crushed.speaker: Hask
line: Brave. Stupid, but brave. Back to work, lancers. You'll fly the next one for a twentieth.

chair.speaker: npc
line: The chair's empty. Somebody has to sit in it.

choices.text: I'll take it. The lance has bled for this ship longer than anyone.

decision.prompt: Put a pilot in the captain's chair

choices.text: It's yours, Tamsin. It always should have been.
Bede keeps the books straight. Let the quartermaster run the ship.

hask.speaker: narrator
line: Corvo Hask is on his knees in the airlock, still smiling.

choices.text: Put him off at Gallows Reach with nothing. Let him start over.
The brig. He stays where we can see him.
Cycle the airlock.
And smash the vat. Nobody owns us again.

hask_after.speaker: narrator
line: Glass and growth fluid across the medical bay. Whoever dies now stays dead.

target.speaker: npc
line: One last job, then. One that ends the running. Where do we hit?

choices.text: The Gallowglass treasury. Vosk has had it coming.
The impounded printer convoy at the customs dock.

end.speaker: narrator
line: The Cadence turns for Gallows Reach.

greet.speaker: npc
line: My favourite lancers. What do you need?
Ah. Trouble or business?

menu.speaker: npc
line: Go on.
Ask.

choices.text: About that vat in the medical bay...
The lance's share is too small.
I'm challenging you for the chair, Hask. By the old law.
Why do you keep sending us to the far side of the ship?
Does anyone on this ship actually like you?
Later.

vat.speaker: npc
line: Flash-grown, quick, quiet. Quite unlawful, so don't tell the Union. I've buried enough good pilots. There: you're in it now.

cut.speaker: npc
line: Shares are what keep three thousand people from each other's throats. Change one, and I'm changing them all. Bring me the holds, and we'll talk.

challenged.speaker: npc
line: The old law. How sweet. Fine. When the time comes, in front of everyone.

fame.speaker: npc
line: Because a ship needs one captain, and the holds have started cheering for four. I like you. I need you. I can't have the holds choosing between us.

bristle.speaker: npc
line: Enough of them to keep the air on. Careful.

farewell.speaker: npc
line: Fly safe. Or at least profitably.

greet.speaker: npc
line: Sit down, lancer. You look like you need soup.
Back again. The usual?

menu.speaker: npc
line: What'll it be?

choices.text: What are people saying?
What do the holds really think of Hask?
Thanks, Wen.

talk.speaker: npc
line: Nothing much. Who's sleeping with whose cousin. Whether the water ration's going down again.

talk_unrest.speaker: npc
line: That Hask is scared of you. That's what they're saying. Not where he can hear it. Yet.

talk_fame.speaker: npc
line: The kids in hold six made little mechs out of ration tins. One of them's you. Hask walked past it this morning and didn't say a word.

talk_ledger.speaker: npc
line: That somebody's been reading the captain's private books. And that what's in them isn't pretty.

hask.speaker: npc
line: He brought three thousand of us out of a dying ship and nobody starved. That buys a lot of patience. It doesn't buy all of it.

farewell.speaker: npc
line: Eat something.

greet.speaker: npc
line: Our lancers. Come, sit. The children want to see your hands; they think pilots have metal ones.

menu.speaker: npc
line: What can the holds do for you?

choices.text: What do the holds need most?

effects.why: the lance asked the families what they needed

choices.text: If it came to it, would the holds stand with us?
Another time, Mother.

needs.speaker: npc
line: Air that doesn't taste of the scrubbers. A school that isn't a cargo container. To be treated like people and not cargo. You can't fix the first two.

stand.speaker: npc
line: We've stood behind captains for two generations. If the lance asks, the holds will stand beside it. Ask carefully.

farewell.speaker: npc
line: Come back for supper.

greet.speaker: npc
line: Lancer.
You again. Pull up a crate.

menu.speaker: npc
line: What is it?

choices.text: How's the crew holding up?
If we moved on Hask, who'd stand with us?

check.consequence: Tamsin shakes her head. "Not yet. They don't trust you enough."

choices.text: Nothing. Carry on.

crew.speaker: npc
line: The old hands are tired and scared. Hask's people are tired and greedy. One of those lasts longer than the other.

rallied.speaker: npc
line: Half the old hands. More, if someone gives them a reason. Leave it with me.

farewell.speaker: npc
line: Watch your back.

lines.text: Welcome back, {name}. Quietly, please. The holds took it hard when you died, and I'd rather they didn't make a saint of you.
Hask means it kindly. He's also already thinking about what the holds will say.
Welcome back, {name}. You don't remember the fight, do you? Good. It wasn't worth remembering.
The vat hisses as it starts the next one. Somebody in the medical bay has started a tally on the wall. Nobody's laughing.
{name}. Your heartbeat is slightly different. I will not tell anyone.

quells.text: At the evening meal Hask thanks "the whole crew" for the lance's last job, and names his own people one by one. Down in the holds, people notice whose names he left out.
Hask gives the next market patrol to his own people and sends the lance to scrub the reactor baffles. "Nobody's too good for the hard jobs," he says. The holds think otherwise.
Hask moves the lance's bunks from the crew deck to the far end of the cargo spine, "closer to the hangar". The families who used to stop by with food have a long walk now. Some make it anyway.
Hask gives a speech in the mess about how no one person keeps a ship alive. Everyone knows who he means. Mother Siddiqui walks out halfway through, and half the holds go with her.

jobs.name: A repair shift
jobs.talk: worked a double shift with Juno Pike's repair crews
jobs.text: Twelve hours in the air scrubbers with Juno Pike's crew. The holds breathe a little easier tonight.
jobs.fail: A coupling blows and the deck loses air for an hour. Nobody's hurt. Pike is furious.

jobs.name: Settle a dispute in the holds
jobs.talk: settled a feud in the holds without anyone getting hurt
jobs.text: Two families, one water ration, one cabin wall. By the end of the night they're sharing both.
jobs.fail: It ends with a punch thrown and a cabin wall kicked in. Hask's people have to break it up.

jobs.name: Guard the markets
jobs.talk: kept the thieves out of the markets
jobs.text: A quiet night in the cargo-bay markets, because everyone could see a lancer standing in the middle of it.
jobs.fail: Three stalls are cleaned out while you're watching the wrong aisle.

side_jobs.title: Escort Run
side_jobs.objective: Escort the Cadence's supply shuttles back from the ice moon.
side_jobs.stakes: The holds eat what those shuttles carry.
side_jobs.question: Do the shuttles get home?

side_jobs.title: Thieves in the Markets
side_jobs.objective: Drive the armed gang out of the cargo-bay markets.
side_jobs.stakes: Families have been robbed at gunpoint.
side_jobs.question: Can the markets be made safe?
side_jobs.enemy: a gang from the Gannet's old crew

side_jobs.title: Salvage for the Holds
side_jobs.objective: Strip the derelict ore tug for hull plate the repair crews need.
side_jobs.stakes: The Cadence's patched holds won't take another winter.
side_jobs.question: What's still alive on the tug?
